issues.title: Windows ARM64 native-codegen tests selected the x64 Zig package
issues.fix: Select Zig package using current OS and architecture; added six-target mapping regression cases.

issues.title: Standalone packaging labels were hard-coded to x64
issues.rootCause: The package script used x64 labels for Windows, Linux, and macOS regardless of host architecture.
issues.fix: Added a validated host target resolver for OS/architecture and platform-specific executable names.
issues.verification: Six target mappings plus unsupported architecture rejection pass in Jest; full package generation was not rerun to avoid overwriting existing release evidence.

issues.title: Release workflow covered only three platform/architecture combinations and CI results were not archived as machine-readable artifacts
issues.rootCause: Workflow matrices and outcome evidence were incomplete.
issues.fix: Configured six release host/target pairs, archived per-run CI outcomes, and preserved container valid/invalid runtime output.
issues.verification: YAML parsing and target triple parsing passed locally; no hosted run was triggered.

issues.title: Container build and execution are uncertified
issues.rootCause: Docker and Podman are unavailable and WSL2 cannot start on this host.
issues.fix: Container workflow records build/runtime outcomes and uploads valid/invalid logs; actual image test remains outstanding.

issues.title: Five required architecture-matched execution environments are unverified
issues.rootCause: Only Windows x64 is available locally; the local-only task did not execute the modified workflows on remote hosted runners.
issues.fix: Configured six-platform CI and release matrices; actual hosted execution remains outstanding.
issues.verification: BLOCKED for Windows ARM64, Linux x64/ARM64, and macOS x64/ARM64.

issues.title: First draft of the new Jest table had a readonly tuple type error
issues.rootCause: An as-const table did not match Jest’s mutable callback tuple typing.
issues.fix: Declared a typed mutable tuple array.
